# Theorem T1, the small-eps tail: ball-arithmetic proof of S(eps) for every real eps in (0, eps_hi]  (generated by experiments/theory3a_run.py)

Round theory3 A.  Statements and their status are in the report text below; the proofs by hand are in the working note THEORY3A.md of the author (outside the repository).  Verifier: `theory3a_tail.verify_tail` (python-flint, 100 bits); chain: `theory_t1b_wide.cover` with `theory3a_chain.verify_fixed`.  The limit object's data (critical points, entry times, duals) are floating-point inputs taken as exact, exactly as in `theory_t1b_rigorous` (not enclosed here).

## U. The eps-free envelope of the dormant coefficient in ball arithmetic

For each eps (the unit with h = 1/kappa a point ball) and a geometric grid of x, the ball enclosure of w(x) is compared with the lower end of C/(s(s^2 - sigma_0^2)) at the ball enclosure of the distance s(x) = lambda - eta(x), for all grid points with s >= 25 (C = 100/3 = 4/(G gamma^2 m), sigma_0 = 20).  "worst" = the largest upper end of w/env (must be <= 1).

| eps | grid points with s>=25 | worst w/env (upper end) |
|---|---|---|
| 1e-2 | 577 | 0.395407830 |
| 1e-4 | 582 | 0.972677625 |
| 1e-6 | 582 | 0.998800278 |
| 1e-8 | 582 | 0.999945179 |
| 1e-12 | 582 | 0.999999882 |
| 1e-16 | 582 | 1.000000000 |
| 1e-20 | 582 | 1.000000000 |
| 1e-24 | 582 | 1.000000000 |

All ratios are <= 1: yes.

## S. How the layer ingredients of S(eps) move with eps

The ingredients of Lemma 3.3 / 4.1 / 5.3 (enclosures at the point eps = 10^e, for the same parameters pi) against the ball of ALL eps <= 1e-24 ("limit").  For an ingredient that enters S as an upper bound (T1, Atr, T2, T3, Env, Tlay, pre, pre_drift) the table uses the upper end of the enclosure, for one that enters as a divisor (kappa, mV) the lower end, for the closed-form positions (x1, w1, xs) the midpoint.  "adverse as eps decreases" = the ingredient gets WORSE for S (an upper-type ingredient larger, a lower-type smaller) as eps decreases, i.e. S(eps_1) does not by itself bound the ingredient at smaller eps; "excess" = the relative amount by which the limit is worse than the value at eps (positive = adverse).  T1, Atr, T2, T3, Env and pre_drift are upper Riemann sums / guards on a fixed number of cells (1500, 3000): their relative discretisation error (about 1e-7 .. 1e-6) limits what the last digits of their direction mean; pre, x1, w1, xs, kappa, mV are closed-form evaluations.

Reading: "adverse" ingredients (pre, T3, Env, kappa, mV) are monotone in the wrong direction by a relative amount proportional to eps (about 1.6 eps for pre), so the value at eps_1 does not bound them at smaller eps; the supremum over eps <= eps_1 is the limit value (eps = 0), which is what the ball [0, h_hi] of Part T encloses.  T1, Atr, Tlay and pre_drift move in the favourable direction (larger at larger eps).
